AF/AFL patients have a higher prevalence of CV comorbidity than patients without AF/AFL, and the incremental cost burden of AF/AF patients with additional risk factor (ARF) (hypertension or diabetes or systemic embolism or stroke/transient ischaemic attack) is largely due to CV-related inpatient cost.

AF/AFL patients are at increased risk of hospitalizations compared to non-AF/AF patients, and that the incremental cost burden of AF/AF patients is primarily driven by CV-related inpatient hospitalization costs.

AF/AFL patients have an increased cost burden, which is even higher in AF/AF patients with ARF.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of ≥1 ARF in AF/AFL patient population is associated with higher healthcare costs and utilization.
the incremental cost burden of AF and AFL in the Medicare population is driven by comorbidity, particularly CV comorbidity.
AF/AFL patients have a high burden on healthcare payers, and that AF/AFL with ≥1 ARFs have an even higher cost burden than AF/AFL patients without ≥1 ARFs.
